title: Playing a recording never blinks
goal: Playing a full-screen Retina recording flickers even when nobody has edited it: a frame the app has not finished reading yet is drawn as empty instead of holding the last picture. Playback should hold the last good frame and read frames fast enough that the picture never blanks.
notes:
Intake detail (the goal as first filed, moved here by triage 2026-09-23): Playback of an untouched full-screen Retina recording flickers (user, 2026-09-23). Root cause, proven by a renderer test in the intake window: (1) MovieClip.swift:193-197 playing(atTimeMS:) swaps the clip to the new frame's ref whether or not it is decoded, and DocumentRenderer.swift:833 drops a layer whose ref is not in ImageStore, so a late frame draws as transparent instead of holding the last frame (video.md claims it holds; no code does). (2) movieFrameLanded (EditorState+Time.swift:210-223) resubmits an identical document, RenderDiff sees no change and renderInteractive (DocumentRenderer.swift:283-287) returns the cached blank frame, so the blank persists for the whole 33ms slot. A timing replay on a real 3456x2234 recording had 22 of 91 ticks blank, alternating 16 times; a 1696x1118 one was fine, so full-size Retina decode cannot keep up.

User: 'When I play back, it's flickering the video! not even edited.'
acceptance: Renderer test: a recording document at a moment whose frame is not decoded, drawn right after one that was, shows the earlier frame's pixels, never transparent
Renderer test: after the missing frame is filed and the landing redraw runs, the new frame's pixels show (the landing redraw is not a no-op)
Core test: given the set of decoded frames, the drawn document uses the newest decoded frame at or before the moment
Playback decodes at preview/canvas size (AVAssetImageGenerator maximumSize or equivalent) and looks ahead enough that a 3456x2234 recording plays with no blank tick in a replay of the real decoder
A walk plays a full-screen Retina recording for 3 seconds, photographs at least 20 moments, and fails if any has the clip area empty

log.note: triage 2026-09-23: goal rewritten in plain language, the old one kept at the top of notes; epic (none) -> video-editing

reproduced: new renderer tests failed on the old renderer (a frame filed under a ref the document already points at, and one re-read bigger, both answered from the cache as the old picture). Timing: the app's decoder (one AVAssetImageGenerator, sequential) takes 39ms median, 59ms p90 per frame on the real 3456x2234 'Recording 2026-09-06 at 22.29.13.mp4', and maximumSize 1200 or 1728 makes NO difference (43ms, 40ms): the cost is the decode. 4 generators side by side read 60 frames in 363ms; AVAssetReader 90 in 376ms.

adversarial pass: a Premiere/QuickTime user expects a late frame to hold, never to blank, and a scrub backwards to keep a picture; both done (newest at-or-before, else nearest after). Export must never use a stand-in or a preview-sized frame: drawn() without framesInHand is unchanged, and DocumentFrames now re-reads full size if the window holds a smaller one. No mock covers playback smoothness; it is behaviour only.

fixed: MovieFramesInHand + drawn(atTimeMS:framesInHand:) in PhotonzCore; renderInteractive compares the bitmap identity of every visible picture layer before trusting RenderDiff; MovieDecoder has 4 lanes per (recording, size); fetcher reads at MovieRef.decodePixelSize(shownScale: zoom*backing*layer scale), 8 ahead while playing, re-reads on zoom. New walk step expectPlaybackNeverBlank; open step opens movies as documents.

verified: playing-a-recording-never-blinks-walk on a synthetic 3456x2234 60fps fixture (decodes at 107ms/frame, harsher than the real ones): 24 of 24 looks drawn, 4 then 6 held a frame up to 3 back. NEGATIVE CONTROL: with hold off, 1 lane, lookahead 3 and the old renderer cache, the same walk FAILED with the clip EMPTY at 15 of 24 looks. Neighbour walks ok: a-recording-is-a-document, hold-on-a-frame, a-frame-of-a-video-comes-out-as-a-picture, an-edited-recording-comes-out-as-a-video, cut-on-the-timeline, transitions-at-a-cut.

default config: the walk has to set next-a-recording-is-a-document, which is off at Next defaults (the user turned it on by hand; their dev app's flags confirm it). The default path is the old recording window, which plays through AVPlayerView and cannot blink this way. Making the editor path default is a-recording-opens-in-the-video-editor-for-real-i, noted there. Full test suite: red only on the known busy-machine export-size flake, also red on clean main (evidence on the-export-size-test-fails-about-one-run-in-thre).

left rough: a frame can still be up to ~3 frames late under load (it holds, never blanks); AVAssetReader sequential decode would be faster still for straight playback but needs its own playback pipeline, not worth a task while holding covers it. Reframe section inset seen in the capture folded into the-video-properties-look-like-the-rest-of-the-d.
